### Page note: https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6802069/
Reader state: complete; relevance: partial
| Fact | Evidence |
|------|----------|
| **Species name** – Kordofan giraffe = *Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum* (a subspecies of the northern giraffe). | “The Kordofan giraffe (_Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum_), a subspecies of the northern giraffe …” |
| **Geographic range within DRC** – Found exclusively in Garamba National Park (NP) and the adjacent hunting reserves: Mondo Missa, Gangala na Bodio, Azande. | “The population of Kordofan giraffe in Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is geographically isolated from all others and only occurs in Garamba National Park (GNP) and its adjacent Hunting Reserves (Mondo Missa, Gangala na Bodio, and Azande).” |
| **Location of Garamba NP** – UNESCO World Heritage Site established 1980, located in north‑eastern DRC (approx. 04°13′N 29°24′E). | “Garamba National Park, a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 1980, is situated in the North East of the DRC… (04°13′N 29°24′E).” |
| **Population estimate (2017)** – 45 Kordofan giraffes (26 females, 19 males). | “The Garamba NP population was estimated to be 45 giraffe at the end of the study …” (also “female‑dominated (26 females: 14 males—…”) |
| **Sex ratio** – 35 % males, 65 % females (male:female ratio 1 : 0.54). | “the sex ratio was female biased (1:0.54) (male 35%, female 65%).” |
| **Age distribution (2017)** – Adult 71.1 %, subadult 17.7 %, juvenile 11.2 %. | “adult dominated… age class ratios observed as 1:0.25:0.16 (adult 71.1%: subadult 17.7%: juvenile 11.2%).” |
| **Study period** – Aerial surveys: 26 Sep 2016 – 17 Aug 2017; GPS collars deployed 24 Jan–3 Feb 2016. | “Population numbers… were gathered between September 26 2016, and August 17, 2017… GPS satellite collars deployed in early 2016.” |
| **Home‑range sizes** – Kerensen 95 % KDE (average 268.8 km²); AKDE (average 934.3 km²). | “average HR of 934.3 km² using AKDE and 268.8 km² using KDE.” |
| **Distribution‐by‑area** – Giraffes mainly in the eastern and southern sectors of Garamba NP; few in northern and western sectors; see Table 2. | “Kordofan giraffe were predominantly observed in the eastern and southern areas of the GNP complex…” and “Table 2” lists individuals by region. |
| **Key individuals (GPS‑collared)** – GIR36M, GIR37F, GIR38M, GIR39M, GIR40M, GIR41M, GIR42F, GIR43F. | Table 1 lists collar names, sexes, ages, areas, lifespan and read counts. |
| **Conservation status** – Critically endangered on IUCN Red List (declined > 85 % in 30 yrs). | “...was added to the IUCN Red List as a critically endangered subspecies (Fennessy & Marais, 2018).” |
| **Population trend** – Decrease from 350 giraffes (1976) to 22 (2012) to 34 (2017), rising to 45 (2017). | “Population numbers… declined… from 350 giraffe in 1976 to a low of 22 giraffe in 2012… increased to 34 giraffe in 2017.” |
| **Management** – Garamba NP/complex managed by African Parks Network in partnership with Institut Congolais pour la Conservation de la Nature (ICCN) since 2005. | “African Parks Network (APN) … has been managing the Garamba complex … since 2005.” |
| **Habitat** – Garamba NP lies in the Sudan–Guinean savannah zone; climate tropical semihumid. | “...located in the Sudan–Guinean savannah zone… climate is tropical semihumid.” |
| **Key references for Kordofan giraffe species** – Fennessy & Marais 2018, IUCN Red List entry. | “Fennessy & Marais, 2018. Giraffa camelopardalis ssp. antiquorum.” |

**Page**  
*Population structure and spatial ecology of Kordofan giraffe in Garamba National Park, Democratic Republic of Congo* (Ecology and Evolution, 2019;9:11395–11405).

**Evidence**  
*As listed in the table above, each bullet cites its exact sentence from the article’s text.*

**Coverage**  
- Time period: 26 Sep 2016 – 17 Aug 2017 (field data); 24 Jan – 3 Feb 2016 (GPS collar deployment).  
- Geographic scope: Garamba NP and adjoining hunting reserves in northeastern DRC.  
- Species: *Giraffa camelopardalis antiquorum* (Kordofan giraffe).  
- Population data: total 45 individuals, sex/age structure, home‑range estimates.  
- Conservation status: IUCN Critically Endangered; trend data 1976–2017.

- Up‑to‑date population numbers beyond 2017.

**Next links**
